newsitem.title: UK: Tate & Lyle no comment on sweetener prices.
newsitem.headline: Tate & Lyle no comment on sweetener prices.

text.p: Tate & Lyle Plc declined comment on Thursday on market talk of pressure on U.S. sweetener prices that has sent its shares sharply lower this week.

A Tate spokesman said the company would not give any view on prices of high fructose syrup, which accounts for some 60 percent of the output of its U.S. unit Staley. "We would never comment in the middle of any commercial negotiations," he said.

In a sharply rising UK stock market, Tate shares were down 2p at 450 by 1622 GMT, extending Wednesday's 15 fall after analysts at NatWest Securities warned that they may cut earnings estimates because of pressure on high fructose prices.
Other analysts have also lowered earnings expectations in recent sessions amid U.S. reports of a squeeze on high fructose prices.
A report in U.S. trade magazine Milling & Baking News said last week: "High fructose prices appeared to be under extreme pressure as bookings for 1997 gained momentum."
It said bookings of high fructose syrup for 1997 had risen in the past week but were "not as heavy as had been anticipated."

The magazine added that pricing was said to have spanned a wide range but was "far lower than a year earlier and refiner predictions," and quoted one baker as saying: "I don't expect refiners to make money in 1997."
